explanation: Take the parent graph (the faint gray curve) and apply the four classic moves at once. h slides it left/right (note x - h moves it RIGHT by h), k slides it up/down, and a stretches it vertically and flips it upside down when negative. The pink dot rides the transformed curve and the warm dot marks the vertex (h, k) so you can see exactly where the parent's anchor point landed after the moves.
bullets: Outside changes (a, k) act vertically; inside changes (h) act horizontally.
Inside moves run 'backwards': x - h shifts RIGHT, x + h shifts LEFT.
a < 0 reflects the graph across the x-axis; |a| > 1 makes it steeper.
